opportunities.name: Compressor Heat Recovery
opportunities.description: Recover low-temperature heat rejected by the main oil-free compressor for sanitary hot water or boiler feedwater preheating.
assumptions: 132 kW main compressor rated power
39% average load from audit context
80% of compressor electrical energy rejected as heat
60% practical capture efficiency
Stack temperature assumed 50°C (not measured)
7300 h/year availability based on shift schedule

opportunities.name: Steam Boiler Economizer
opportunities.description: Install a flue gas economizer on the steam boiler stack to preheat boiler feedwater, reducing fuel consumption.
assumptions: 1840 kW total boiler nominal output (2 × 920 kW)
70% average load factor from billing data
7% of input energy lost in flue gas (stack temperature not directly measured)
60% heat recovery effectiveness from economizer
Stack temperature assumed 160°C — requires measurement before final engineering

opportunities.name: Automatic Blowdown / TDS Heat Recovery
opportunities.description: Install a blowdown heat exchanger and flash vessel to recover thermal energy from continuous boiler blowdown water.
assumptions: 1840 kW boiler rated output
70% average load factor
4% blowdown heat loss fraction (TDS control not directly measured)
50% practical recovery via flash vessel + heat exchanger
Blowdown rate assumed 4% of steam production — requires TDS measurement

opportunities.name: Condensate Recovery Improvement
opportunities.description: Increase hot condensate return rate to the boiler to reduce fresh water heating and chemical dosing requirements.
assumptions: Current condensate return rate assumed ~40% — not measured
Target return rate 70%+ after intervention
3% of total thermal output lost as non-returned condensate
50% effective heat recovery improvement
Measurement confidence is LOW — condensate flow not instrumented

opportunities.name: Chiller Condenser Heat Recovery
opportunities.description: Recover low-grade heat rejected at chiller condenser for preheating domestic hot water or process water. High potential but low temperature and integration complexity.
assumptions: 820 kW total chiller capacity (condensing side ≈ input + cooling)
50% average load factor during cooling season
100% of condenser rejection is recoverable in principle
Only 30% practical capture — low temperature (35–45°C) limits use
Demand validation required — not guaranteed on this site
High CAPEX due to heat pump or dedicated HEX + piping required
requires_measurement: availability of nearby hot water demand

opportunities.name: Trigeneration Heat Allocation Optimization
opportunities.description: Detect and reduce situations where recovered cogen heat is available but boilers still run unnecessarily. Digital optimization of heat dispatch.
assumptions: 1270 kW trigeneration engine thermal output at rated power
20% of thermal output wasted due to dispatch inefficiency (estimated)
8030 h/year engine availability based on telemetry
20% additional effective heat capture through dispatch optimization
Digital solution only — no new heat exchangers required initially
requires_measurement: recovered heat meter at cogen hot water circuit

opportunities.name: Beta Zone Heat Recovery Extension
opportunities.description: Extend hot water distribution to Beta production zone to offset local gas or electric heating. Strategic but piping feasibility unknown.
assumptions: 400 kW estimated available hot water thermal capacity
50% load factor based on seasonal heating demand
50% fraction of hot water allocated for Beta extension
50% capture efficiency — piping losses and distance accounted for
4380 h/year — heating season only, not year-round
Beta zone demand profile and exact piping route not validated
requires_measurement: existing hot water supply capacity at Beta boundary

opportunities.name: Hot Surface Insulation
opportunities.description: Insulate bare or under-insulated hot pipes, valves, and equipment surfaces to reduce standby heat losses.
assumptions: 100 kW estimated surface radiation loss — low confidence until thermographic survey
100% availability — surfaces are always hot during operation
50% of surface loss is recoverable through insulation
70% insulation effectiveness (standard mineral wool insulation)
Measurement confidence is LOW — surface area and temperatures not formally measured
